overview: This two-page Department of State list of papers indexes records filed under Japanese railways, principally from 1930 to 1939. Its entries cover railway construction at Nagasaki, Japanese government railway reports, the Echigo and Yamate Express Tramway scandal, leadership turmoil at the South Manchuria Railway, plans for a rail tunnel between Honshu and Kyushu, proposed Chinese purchases of American railway materials, and State Department and Reconstruction Finance Corporation deliberations over selling Lehigh Valley locomotives to Japanese interests. Several entries point researchers to related decimal-file classifications rather than reproducing the underlying documents.

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers concerning railways in Japan
subfiles.about: An archival index summarizes and cross-references Japanese railway records dating chiefly from 1930 through 1939.
subfiles.summary: The list indexes reports on the Nagasaki railway extension, annual publications of the Japanese Department of Railways, the Echigo and Yamate Express Tramway scandal, the South Manchuria Railway leadership controversy, and plans for an undersea connection between Honshu and Kyushu. It also identifies a proposal for the Chinese Ministry of Railways to buy American railway materials on long-term credit. The final group of entries concerns discussions among the State Department, Reconstruction Finance Corporation, and Lehigh Valley Railroad over selling locomotives to Japanese interests. Several matters are cross-referenced to files 894.00 P.R., 893.01, and 894.01; the last entry is largely illegible in the OCR.

interest: The document is valuable primarily as a finding aid: it reveals how the State Department grouped railway construction, administrative reporting, political scandals, foreign procurement, and export-control questions within a single subject file. Its cross-references show how railway matters migrated among political-reporting, Chinese affairs, and commercial-control classifications. Particularly useful is the sequence concerning Lehigh Valley locomotives, which captures growing official sensitivity toward sales to Japanese interests before the Pacific War, while the Shimonoseki tunnel entry records early planning for the eventual Honshu–Kyushu rail link.
